case.case_title: Perera and Another v. Cyril Ranatunga, Secretary Defence and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (1993) 1 Sri L.R. 39

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the promotion scheme for Senior Authorised Officers based on seniority and merit violated Article 12(1) by denying equal protection of the law to the petitioners who were overlooked for promotion in favor of junior officers.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners argued that the promotion scheme was discriminatory, arbitrary, and lacked proper criteria and publicity, resulting in denial of equal protection of the law under Article 12(1). They claimed they were unfairly overlooked despite superior seniority, qualifications, and service records.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that promotions were made on the basis of seniority and merit, assessed by an Interview Board using a marking scheme and subjective evaluation of competence, knowledge, and personality. They argued the appointments were lawful and in the best interests of the department.
key_facts: Promotion to Senior Authorised Officer was based on seniority and merit, assessed by an Interview Board chaired by the Controller of Immigration and Emigration.
The marking scheme allocated 15 marks for seniority, 10 for personality, 30 for work performance (detections), 25 for knowledge of law and practice, and 20 for problem-solving capacity.
Petitioners had higher seniority, better educational qualifications, and unblemished service records compared to junior officers promoted over them.
The marking scheme was not publicized in advance and was applied arbitrarily with subjective criteria.
Interviews lasted only a few minutes and did not adequately assess knowledge or problem-solving skills.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(1) as guaranteeing equality before the law and equal protection, which includes equality of opportunity in public employment. The principle of seniority and merit must be applied fairly, with rational criteria and publicity to avoid arbitrariness and discrimination. Merit includes both positive competence and absence of demerit, and seniority must be given meaningful weight unless justified otherwise.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the promotion scheme deficient in criteria and weightage, especially undervaluing seniority (only 15%), and relying on subjective, arbitrary, and non-publicized methods. The petitioners were denied equal protection as the scheme and its application lacked rational justification and fairness, resulting in discriminatory treatment favoring junior officers without sufficient basis.
principles_established: Equality before the law under Article 12(1) includes equality of opportunity in public employment.
Promotions based on seniority and merit require clear, rational, and publicized criteria.
Subjective and arbitrary discretion in promotions violates the rule of law and equal protection.
Seniority must be given meaningful weight unless special skills or demerit justify otherwise.
The burden is on the state to justify any classification or deviation from seniority.
precedents_cited: Buddhan Choudhry v. State of Bihar AIR 1955 S.C. 191
Ram Krishna Dalmia v. Justice Tendolkar AIR 1958 S.C. 538
Elmore Perera v. Major Montague Jayawickrema (1985) 1 Sri LR 285
Eheliyagoda v. J.E.D.B. and others F.R.D. Vol. 1 p. 243
Jaisinghani v. Union of India AIR 1967 S.C. 1427
State of Mysore v. S.R. Jayaram AIR 1968 S.C. 346
State of Mysore v. Krishna Murthy AIR 1973 S.C. 1147

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioners' fundamental rights under Article 12(1) were infringed by the impugned promotions. The appointments of the junior officers over the petitioners were set aside, and the respondents were directed to make fresh appointments consistent with Article 12.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Set aside the appointments of the 3rd to 6th respondents and directed fresh appointments according to law; awarded costs of Rs. 2500/- to each petitioner.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court's reasoning as it guarantees equality before the law and equal protection, which the court found was violated by the arbitrary and discriminatory promotion scheme. The court relied on this clause to invalidate the impugned promotions and order fresh appointments.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found that the promotion scheme gave only 15% weight to seniority, was arbitrary, unpredictable, and unguided by any known rule or principle, and that the petitioners were denied equal protection of the law and unequally treated on a basis which cannot be rationally justified.
